newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles council amends $4 bln budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles council amends $4 bln budget plan.

text.p: The Los Angeles city council adopted changes to Mayor Richard Riordan's $4 billion budget plan for fiscal year 1997-1998, boosting park, library and economic development spending, city officials said.

The amendments, approved by the city council on Monday, included a $1.5 million boost in funding for council offices, $1 million to expand park staffing, $1.2 million of additional library funding, and $500,000 to set up new business improvement districts.
Riordan has 10 days to veto any of the amendments before returning the spending plan to the council for final action.
The mayor's $4 billion spending plan -- $50 million smaller than last year's budget -- contained a reserve of $30 million, and seeks no new taxes.
